findings.body: A `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of `multiprocessing.Process`, so the hung worker is left running while a replacement is started for the same shards. If the old worker recovers, both can flush the same Redis queues, causing duplicate Kafka output, while permanently hung workers leak resources.
findings.failure_mode: The old shard worker remains active and untracked after its entry in `self.processes` is overwritten.
findings.impact: A `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of `multiprocessing.Process`, so the hung worker is left running while a replacement is started for the same shards. If the old worker recovers, both can flush the same Redis queues, causing duplicate Kafka output, while permanently hung workers leak resources.
findings.root_cause: The restart path uses a type check that does not recognize processes created by the explicit spawn context.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify subprocesses using `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` or distinguish them from `threading.Thread`, then kill and join the old subprocess before starting its replacement.
findings.title: Hung spawn workers are replaced without being killed
findings.trigger: A production flusher created through `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` remains alive but stops updating its health timestamp long enough to be classified as hung.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 254 shows `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` but processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` (line 105) which returns `SpawnProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`. The isinstance check fails, so hung spawn workers won't be killed before replacement.

findings.body: The class documentation claims each shard receives a process, while the implementation explicitly groups multiple shards into each available process, misleading operators about isolation and expected parallelism.
findings.evidence: Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.
findings.failure_mode: Operational expectations about worker count and shard isolation do not match runtime behavior.
findings.impact: The class documentation claims each shard receives a process, while the implementation explicitly groups multiple shards into each available process, misleading operators about isolation and expected parallelism.
findings.root_cause: The documentation describes the uncapped topology and ignores the newly introduced process limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that the flusher creates up to `max_processes` workers and distributes assigned shards among them, with one worker per shard only when the limit permits.
findings.title: The flusher documentation contradicts process sharing
findings.trigger: A caller configures `max_processes` below the number of assigned shards, including the CLI default of one process.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 32 states 'Creates one process per shard' but lines 60-66 show `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` and shards are distributed across processes. Documentation contradicts implementation when max_processes < shard count.

findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` emits the value under `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` emits the same value under `shards`, preventing consistent filtering and grouping across the two timers.
findings.failure_mode: Metrics for adjacent stages cannot be correlated through a common tag without metric-specific query logic.
findings.impact: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` emits the value under `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` emits the same value under `shards`, preventing consistent filtering and grouping across the two timers.
findings.root_cause: The same `shard_tag` dimension was assigned inconsistent singular and plural metric keys.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one tag key, preferably `shards` because the value may contain several shard IDs, and use it consistently for all newly tagged flusher metrics.
findings.title: Related flusher timers use different tag names for the same dimension
findings.trigger: Telemetry is queried or dashboarded by the shard assignment dimension across the produce and wait-produce stages.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 195 uses tag `shard` while line 199 uses tag `shards` for the same `shard_tag` value. This inconsistency prevents unified metric querying across produce and wait_produce stages.

pr.body:
Refs STREAM-266

Compression helped a lot bring the time on the main thread down. We now think we can scale down the consumers. However, we also need to ensure the flusher can keep up. So let's make the flusher spawn a process per redis shard. 

We think this is easier to do than making the process_spans/insert_spans multiprocessed. Over time we can offload mroe things like statistics/metrics to the flusher, and keep the main thread minimal.
pr.title: ref(span-buffer): Introduce multiprocessed flusher

raw_findings.body: The loop exits without terminating any remaining workers. Blocked workers can survive after the strategy's join returns and may continue holding resources or producing segments during shutdown.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Only processes visited before the deadline are considered for termination; all subsequent process entries are skipped.
raw_findings.impact: The loop exits without terminating any remaining workers. Blocked workers can survive after the strategy's join returns and may continue holding resources or producing segments during shutdown.
raw_findings.root_cause: The shared timeout controls both waiting and whether later processes receive mandatory cleanup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not break out of the cleanup loop when the deadline expires. Stop waiting, but continue through every remaining process and terminate any that are still alive.
raw_findings.title: Timed joins can leave later flusher processes running
raw_findings.trigger: `join(timeout=...)` reaches its deadline before iterating over every flusher process, for example because `next_step.join(timeout)` consumed the timeout or an early worker is blocked.

raw_findings.body: The negative count produces an empty `process_to_shards_map`; assigning the first shard then raises `KeyError`, so the consumer cannot start.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Shard-to-process allocation indexes a process map containing no entries.
raw_findings.impact: The negative count produces an empty `process_to_shards_map`; assigning the first shard then raises `KeyError`, so the consumer cannot start.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly exposed process-count option accepts arbitrary integers even though the allocation logic requires a positive count.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `click.IntRange(min=1)` and also validate `max_processes >= 1` in `SpanFlusher` for non-CLI callers.
raw_findings.title: Negative flusher process counts crash consumer initialization
raw_findings.trigger: The process-spans consumer is started with a negative value such as `--flusher-processes=-1`.

raw_findings.body: Every per-process buffer queries memory information for the same complete Redis cluster on each submission. With one process per shard this multiplies cluster-wide INFO requests and manager-side Redis clients by the process count without changing the calculated utilization ratio.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A constant-time cluster health check becomes O(number of flusher processes) network work.
raw_findings.impact: Every per-process buffer queries memory information for the same complete Redis cluster on each submission. With one process per shard this multiplies cluster-wide INFO requests and manager-side Redis clients by the process count without changing the calculated utilization ratio.
raw_findings.root_cause: Cluster-wide monitoring is performed by iterating shard-specific buffer objects even though all of them reference the same Redis service.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Retain a single manager-level buffer or Redis client and call `get_memory_info()` once per submission; reserve the per-process buffers for child flushing only.
raw_findings.title: Memory backpressure queries the entire Redis cluster once per worker
raw_findings.trigger: Memory backpressure is enabled with `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0` and the flusher is configured with multiple processes.

raw_findings.body: Queue cardinalities are collected through a separate Redis pipeline for each process buffer instead of the former single pipeline across all assigned shards, multiplying network round trips at every submission.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Monitoring incurs O(number of workers) Redis round trips rather than one batched request.
raw_findings.impact: Queue cardinalities are collected through a separate Redis pipeline for each process buffer instead of the former single pipeline across all assigned shards, multiplying network round trips at every submission.
raw_findings.root_cause: Parent-side monitoring was partitioned along with child-side flushing even though it does not need process isolation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a manager-level buffer containing all assigned shards and call `record_stored_segments()` once, or batch all shard cardinality commands into one pipeline.
raw_findings.title: Queue-size monitoring adds one Redis pipeline round trip per worker
raw_findings.trigger: `submit` runs while multiple flusher processes are configured.

validated_findings.impact: Queue cardinalities are collected through a separate Redis pipeline for each process buffer instead of the former single pipeline across all assigned shards, multiplying network round trips at every submission.
validated_findings.root_cause: Parent-side monitoring was partitioned along with child-side flushing even though it does not need process isolation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a manager-level buffer containing all assigned shards and call `record_stored_segments()` once, or batch all shard cardinality commands into one pipeline.
validated_findings.title: Queue-size monitoring adds one Redis pipeline round trip per worker
validated_findings.trigger: `submit` runs while multiple flusher processes are configured.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 269-270 show iteration over `self.buffers.values()` calling `record_stored_segments()` on each. Per buffer.py:357-364, this creates a pipeline per buffer. Multiple buffers means multiple pipelines instead of one batched request.

validated_findings.body: Providing `produce_to_pipe` selects `threading.Thread`, so no changed test covers spawn-process construction, pickling, process liveness checks, or subprocess cleanup. Spawn-specific regressions can pass CI and fail only in production.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Tests validate shard-map bookkeeping but not the production execution and lifecycle path.
validated_findings.impact: Providing `produce_to_pipe` selects `threading.Thread`, so no changed test covers spawn-process construction, pickling, process liveness checks, or subprocess cleanup. Spawn-specific regressions can pass CI and fail only in production.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test-only output callback changes the worker implementation from subprocesses to threads while the feature under review is multiprocessing.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test using the production process branch, with the Kafka producer and process target suitably mocked, and cover startup, unhealthy-worker replacement, and shutdown for at least two spawn workers.
validated_findings.title: The new multiprocess behavior is tested only through threads
validated_findings.trigger: The test suite exercises the newly added multi-worker configuration.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 101 shows `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` which per flusher.py:106-108 causes `make_process = threading.Thread` instead of spawn Process. The test exercises thread path, not the production multiprocessing path being added.

validated_findings.body: The call provides no time for the flusher thread to observe the drift change. If the scheduler does not run that thread before `step.join()` sets the stop flag, the test can fail nondeterministically without producing a message.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Thread scheduling, rather than the behavior under test, determines whether output exists before shutdown.
validated_findings.impact: The call provides no time for the flusher thread to observe the drift change. If the scheduler does not run that thread before `step.join()` sets the stop flag, the test can fail nondeterministically without producing a message.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test attempts to wait using the exact function it globally replaced with a no-op.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Synchronize on an event or poll for `messages` with a retained real sleep function; alternatively patch only the flusher's idle wait rather than the global `time.sleep`.
validated_findings.title: The added synchronization sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op
validated_findings.trigger: `test_basic` reaches the added sleep after having replaced `time.sleep` with `lambda _: None` earlier in the same test.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 15 patches `time.sleep` to no-op, then line 62 calls `time.sleep(0.1)` expecting synchronization. The patched sleep does nothing, making the synchronization ineffective and test potentially flaky.

validated_findings.body: The class documentation claims each shard receives a process, while the implementation explicitly groups multiple shards into each available process, misleading operators about isolation and expected parallelism.
validated_findings.evidence: Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Operational expectations about worker count and shard isolation do not match runtime behavior.
validated_findings.impact: The class documentation claims each shard receives a process, while the implementation explicitly groups multiple shards into each available process, misleading operators about isolation and expected parallelism.
validated_findings.root_cause: The documentation describes the uncapped topology and ignores the newly introduced process limit.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Document that the flusher creates up to `max_processes` workers and distributes assigned shards among them, with one worker per shard only when the limit permits.
validated_findings.title: The flusher documentation contradicts process sharing
validated_findings.trigger: A caller configures `max_processes` below the number of assigned shards, including the CLI default of one process.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 32 states 'Creates one process per shard' but lines 60-66 show `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` and shards are distributed across processes. Documentation contradicts implementation when max_processes < shard count.

validated_findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` emits the value under `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` emits the same value under `shards`, preventing consistent filtering and grouping across the two timers.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Metrics for adjacent stages cannot be correlated through a common tag without metric-specific query logic.
validated_findings.impact: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` emits the value under `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` emits the same value under `shards`, preventing consistent filtering and grouping across the two timers.
validated_findings.root_cause: The same `shard_tag` dimension was assigned inconsistent singular and plural metric keys.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Choose one tag key, preferably `shards` because the value may contain several shard IDs, and use it consistently for all newly tagged flusher metrics.
validated_findings.title: Related flusher timers use different tag names for the same dimension
validated_findings.trigger: Telemetry is queried or dashboarded by the shard assignment dimension across the produce and wait-produce stages.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 195 uses tag `shard` while line 199 uses tag `shards` for the same `shard_tag` value. This inconsistency prevents unified metric querying across produce and wait_produce stages.
